title: Partnering with Corma: Closing the Defensive Cybersecurity Gap
gist: Sequoia is leading the seed round of Corma, a startup training a defense-specific foundation model because logs/telemetry data and open-ended anomaly hunting are out of distribution for general-purpose frontier models, while agentic AI (including Anthropic's Mythos discovering zero-days) has made offense cheap and scalable. The core empirical hook: in Corma's red/blue simulations a defender model failed to find a backdoor 78% of the time even when it was an identical copy of the model that planted it, implying attackers structurally win at equal model quality.

insights.claim: In red/blue team simulations run by the cybersecurity startup Corma, where an attacker plants a hidden backdoor and a defender hunts for it, the defender failed 78% of the time even when the defender was an identical copy of the model that planted the backdoor.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: The single hardest number in the piece: it argues that simply pointing the same frontier model at defense does not close the gap, so incumbent SOC vendors bolting a general LLM onto their product are structurally disadvantaged versus defense-trained models.
insights.quote: The defender failed to find the backdoor 78% of the time, even when the defender was an identical copy of the very same model that planted it.

insights.claim: Holding model quality constant, attackers structurally retain the advantage in cybersecurity, so the only counter to improving offensive scaling laws is building better scaling laws specifically for defense.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Frames security spend as a permanent AI-capex race rather than a one-time upgrade cycle, supporting a structurally rising security budget line for enterprises.
insights.quote: The only answer to scaling laws on offense is better scaling laws on defense.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Mythos-class models can discover and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities, and an explosion in reported CVEs has followed the arrival of agentic AI and these models.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: CVE disclosure volume is a tradable leading indicator of patch-management and vulnerability-management demand; watch it as the tape for this whole category.
insights.quote: Anthropic’s Mythos can discover and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities.

themes.theme: Why defense is out of distribution

insights.claim: Defensive security data lives in logs, events, traces and telemetry, a modality that barely appears in LLM pretraining corpora, and defense requires open-ended anomaly hunting across vast normal-looking activity rather than the goal-directed reasoning that offense uses.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A clean mental model for which AI verticals resist general-model commoditization: the ones whose data modality is absent from web-scale pretraining and whose task is open-ended search rather than objective-directed.
insights.quote: In short, defense is out of distribution for general-purpose frontier models: neither the data nor the intuition it requires is well-represented in training.
insights.locator: The relevant data lives in logs, events

insights.claim: Frontier labs racing toward AGI will not detour to overhaul their training pipelines for defensive cybersecurity, leaving the capability gap open for a specialist to fill.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: This is the load-bearing assumption of the investment; if a major lab does ship a defense-tuned model, the specialist's moat collapses, so treat lab roadmaps as the key falsification signal.
insights.quote: In the race toward AGI, we cannot expect the frontier labs to take the detour of overhauling their training pipelines for defensive cybersecurity.

insights.claim: Cybersecurity is framed as a two-player, zero-sum game with a clean reward signal (breached or not) and an unlimited supply of games, making it the same paradigm in which reinforcement learning and self-play previously produced superhuman results in Go and chess.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A screening test for where RL will actually deliver superhuman AI products: verifiable reward plus unlimited simulated environments, which points to security, trading and formal verification over open-ended knowledge work.
insights.quote: Cybersecurity, like Go or chess, is a two-player, zero-sum game with a clean reward (were you breached or not?) and an endless supply of games to play.
insights.locator: Corma founder and CEO Alon Pluda

insights.claim: Corma trains via large-scale reinforcement learning inside simulated cybersecurity environments that replicate real enterprise networks including their tools, telemetry and noise, and claims the resulting model outperforms general-purpose foundation models at much lower per-token inference cost.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Simulated enterprise environments become the scarce asset in vertical AI; whoever owns a high-fidelity environment generator owns the RL data flywheel, a pattern worth scanning for in other verticals.
insights.quote: large-scale reinforcement learning across cybersecurity environments that replicate real enterprise networks, with all their tools, telemetry and noise

insights.claim: A vertically integrated, sovereign-AI security vendor that owns its own model weights escapes the cybersecurity-usage restrictions that closed model labs impose on their APIs, and avoids the always-on inference bills that continuous monitoring generates.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Closed labs' acceptable-use policies on security tooling are an underappreciated structural subsidy to open-weight and self-trained vendors; check any AI security vendor's dependency on a third-party API before underwriting its margins.
insights.quote: Owning the model weights matters (they aren’t subject to restrictions on cybersecurity-related usage set by the closed model labs).
insights.locator: In the cat-and-mouse game of cybersecurity

insights.claim: Corma's model is productized as an agentic "Security Workforce" filling roles across security operations, identity management, cloud and network security, and is already deployed at Fortune 500 companies and large enterprises in healthcare, finance, critical infrastructure and retail.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: The pricing unit is a security headcount replacement rather than seats or data volume, which threatens the per-GB ingestion model that SIEM and MDR vendors monetize.
insights.quote: They are on the job at Fortune 500 companies and large enterprises across healthcare, finance, critical infrastructure, retail and more.
insights.locator: deployed and productized as an agentic Security Workforce

insights.claim: In one customer deployment, the agent uncovered, contained and remediated an active attacker campaign within its first hour on the job that the customer's own security team had missed for 52 days.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Attacker dwell time is the metric this category will be sold on; if agents compress 52 days to one hour at scale, cyber insurance loss assumptions and MDR retainer pricing both need repricing.
insights.quote: within its first hour on the job, Corma uncovered, contained and remediated an active attacker campaign inside a customer’s network that their security team had missed for 52 days
insights.locator: In another instance, within its first hour
